stories.headline: Albanese delivers rare national address warning of tough months ahead due to Middle East war and fuel crisis
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used a rare televised address to warn Australians that 'months ahead may not be easy' due to the global energy shock from the US-Iran war. The address urged fuel conservation and calm but was criticized for lacking detail on new measures.

stories.headline: RBA bans card surcharges in payment system overhaul expected to save consumers $1.6 billion annually
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank announced it will prohibit surcharges on debit and credit cards from October 2026, part of broader payment system reforms. Business groups warn the costs will be passed on through higher prices.

stories.summary: The Prime Minister unveiled long-awaited gambling reforms including caps on TV ads and stadium bans, but stopped short of the total advertising ban recommended by the landmark Murphy report. Critics say the measures are insufficient.

stories.summary: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor used his right of reply to criticize the Prime Minister's national address as lacking detail and clarity on the fuel crisis. Taylor called for faster development of domestic energy projects and accused the government of poor crisis management.

stories.summary: Reserve Bank minutes showed the board was split on whether to raise rates in March, with members agreeing further tightening would likely be needed but disagreeing on timing. The Iran war has complicated the monetary policy outlook.

stories.summary: Foreign Minister Penny Wong participated in virtual talks with over 40 countries to discuss diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Iran conflict. Australia ruled out offensive military action.
